identification: H. McHugh (McHugh Pottery, Launceston) Tasmanian art pottery squat vase with flared neck, brown and amber streaked drip glaze. Base incised H. McHugh Tasmania and a shape number (reads 13 or 18). Heavy crazing, and photo 3 shows a glaze spot loss with radiating flaking on the body. Roughly 12 to 15cm high judging by proportions (size not stated).

No web searches run: local databases already hold about 100 same-maker sold results from Gowans and Armitage in the last 7 months, so more web work adds little. Rough range: typical signed McHugh vase 40 to 180 hammer, median about 120; small vases with chips or cracks 25 to 100, with exceptions at 180 for chip to base. eBay sold prices not checkable.
viewing_check: Check size (height), shape number on base, whether the chip spot is a through-glaze flake or just a surface loss, any hairline cracks running from it, and whether crazing is stained. Brown and amber drip is a common colourway; look for any dated mark (1934) or unusual form.
